correctness.rationale: For \(g\equiv0\), the source proximal-parameter decrease test is automatic, hence \(\mu_k=\mu\). Inside \(|x|\le\mu\lambda\), soft thresholding gives \(x^+=0\) and \(\eta=x/\mu\). In one dimension the source coefficients satisfy \(\beta d=\gamma y\) identically whenever their common denominator is defined, so \(d=-\eta\). On the claimed basin the source first-stage inequality accepts \(t=1\) because \(|x|\le\mu\lambda/T\), and Armijo accepts \(\alpha=1\) because \(|x|\le\mu\lambda/\delta\). This yields the exact contraction \(x_{k+1}=(1-1/\mu)x_k\). Along that path the corrected denominator is \(d^2(1/\mu+\nu)>0\), so the algebra never divides by zero.

originality.rationale: The primary full text was inspected at the forward-backward residual, proximal-parameter rule, three-term direction, corrected curvature vector, two-stage line search, convergence discussion, and LASSO experiments. Earlier forward-backward identification literature covers finite manifold identification by proximal-gradient-type updates, while the classical three-term Hestenes--Stiefel paper covers smooth descent directions. Neither inspected line implies the source-specific phenomenon that a composite NCG line-search branch can repeatedly bypass a proximal point already equal to the minimizer. Source-specific database and literature searches found no equivalent statement.
residual_risks: Relaxed forward-backward literature may contain analogous examples of failed finite identification under under-relaxation, although no source-specific PNCG implication was located.
The source uses tolerance-based termination in experiments; the exact-stationarity non-identification result should not be read as a claim of endless practical execution.
The construction is scalar and does not classify support identification in higher-dimensional coupled problems.

value.rationale: The primary method is motivated by composite and sparse optimization and explicitly benchmarks on LASSO. In that setting, finite support identification is a structurally important benefit of proximal methods. The finding shows that the hybrid line-search branch can discard an exact proximal hit, identifies a complete source-compatible basin where this happens at every iteration, and gives the exact slowdown factor \(1-1/\mu\), which can approach one. This supplies a concrete design boundary between the acceleration branch and the fallback proximal branch rather than a routine scalar exercise.
